correctness.rationale: The prism width splits exactly into the planar base width times the horizontal component of the direction plus the absolute vertical component. The spherical coordinate Z is uniform on [-1,1], giving three elementary scalar expectations. Cauchy perimeter gives the first planar width moment. The second planar width moment is the squared-support moment of the difference body, which is a regular n-gon for even n and a regular 2n-gon for odd n with explicitly determined radii. A one-cone integral of R^2 cos^2(t) gives the two branches. The bundled checker independently replays direct planar and spatial width computations.

value.rationale: Uniform n-gonal prisms form one of the two canonical infinite series of convex uniform polyhedra. A closed exact second-width-moment formula for every n is a natural family-level classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The result also exposes a reusable product decomposition and a geometric parity split through planar difference bodies.
